answer: Grader-consensus triangulation resists sybils: three independent panels drawn from DISJOINT trust regions grade the same sample, and an answer or grader flagged by cross-panel disagreement is escalated — a summit of three vantage points no single ring can occupy. A colluding cluster can capture at most one panel; the prism of three disjoint draws refracts its bias into visible disagreement. Where the three panels converge, the verdict stands; where one spirals off from the other two, that outlier panel's graders are the flagged collusion signal.
